title: Uganda Independence from Britain
note: October 9, 1962 confirmed; Obote as PM, Mutesa II as ceremonial President confirmed. Note: Mutesa II was elected ceremonial President in November 1963, not on independence day itself.

title: First Post-Independence Elections
note: UPC-KY coalition confirmed; UPC 43 seats, KY 24, DP 24 confirmed. Coalition tensions accurately described.

title: Uganda Joins the Commonwealth and UN
note: Commonwealth and UN membership confirmed. OAU founding in 1963 confirmed. No contradicting evidence found.

title: Mutiny of Ugandan Army Over Pay
note: January 22, 1964 mutiny at Jinja confirmed; British troops (Scots Guards/Staffordshire) deployed; pay and Africanization demands confirmed.

title: Gold Smuggling Scandal Rocks Obote Government
note: March 16, 1965 parliamentary motion by Daudi Ochieng confirmed; gold/ivory/cash from Congo confirmed; Obote and Amin named. Parliament suspension confirmed.

title: Obote Suspends Constitution and Attacks Kabaka's Palace
note: Constitution suspended February 24, 1966; Mengo palace stormed May 24, 1966 by Amin's forces; Mutesa II fled to Britain confirmed.

title: Pigeon-Hole Constitution Centralizes Power
note: 1967 constitution promulgated September 8, 1967; 'pigeon-hole' label refers to the 1966 interim constitution; 1967 text abolished kingdoms and created executive presidency — all confirmed.

title: Assassination Attempt on Obote
note: December 19, 1969 attack at Lugogo Stadium confirmed. Minor inaccuracy: wound was through the cheek/teeth, not 'in the jaw'. Opposition parties banned afterward confirmed.

title: Idi Amin Military Coup
note: January 25, 1971 confirmed; Obote at Commonwealth summit in Singapore confirmed; broad initial popular support including from Buganda confirmed.

title: Amin's Massacre of Acholi and Langi Soldiers
note: Systematic killings of Acholi and Langi soldiers after the coup widely documented. Thousands killed in barracks confirmed by multiple historical sources.

title: Expulsion of Ugandan Asians
note: August 4, 1972 order confirmed; 90-day deadline confirmed; ~80,000 figure confirmed (23,000 had citizenship accepted). 'Divine vision' claim confirmed. Economic devastation confirmed.

title: Economic Nationalization Following Asian Expulsion
note: 5,655 farms/ranches/estates figure confirmed by Wikipedia. 'Economic war' program confirmed. Collapse of commercial sector confirmed.

title: Diplomatic Rupture with Britain and Israel
note: Expulsion of Israeli advisers in 1972 and pivot to Libya/Palestinians confirmed. Rupture with Britain over Asian expulsion confirmed. OAU anti-Israel stance confirmed.

title: Reign of Terror — State Research Bureau Killings
note: SRB and Public Safety Unit atrocities confirmed. 100,000–500,000 death estimate confirmed across historical sources. 1971–1979 reign of terror confirmed.

title: Amin Declares Uganda an Islamic Republic
note: Amin cultivated Islamic ties and received Libyan/Saudi support — confirmed. However, no strong evidence Uganda was formally declared an 'Islamic Republic' (Amin's Uganda remained majority Christian with no formal state religion change). Description likely conflates political posturing with a formal declaration.

title: Entebbe Hostage Crisis
note: Air France hijack June 27, 1976 confirmed (not 'June 1976' in full — raid was July 3-4). Sayeret Matkal confirmed as primary assault unit. 102 of 105 hostages rescued; 3 died confirmed. Minor: description says 'over 100 Jewish and Israeli hostages' — total was 105 non-crew hostages.

title: Murder of Archbishop Janani Luwum
note: February 16, 1977 arrest; death announced as car accident but body was bullet-riddled confirmed. Murder on Amin's orders confirmed. International condemnation confirmed.

title: Uganda Invades Tanzania — Kagera Salient
note: October 1978 invasion confirmed; ~1,800 sq km territory confirmed; Amin's annexation announcement confirmed; ~1,500 Tanzanian civilians killed confirmed.

title: Tanzania-Uganda War — Amin Overthrown
note: Counter-invasion January 1979 confirmed; Kampala fell April 10, 1979 per Wikipedia (event says April 11 — minor discrepancy). Amin fled to Libya then Saudi Arabia; died 2003 confirmed.

title: Post-Amin Transitional Governments
note: Yusuf Lule, then Godfrey Binaisa succession confirmed. Continued instability and competing factions confirmed.

title: Controversial Elections Return Obote to Power
note: December 1980 elections confirmed as widely condemned as fraudulent; Obote declared winner; Museveni's UPM alleged rigging; directly triggered Bush War insurgency confirmed.

title: Bush War Begins — Museveni's NRA Insurgency
note: February 1981 guerrilla start confirmed; Luwero Triangle confirmed; 27 fighters claim is consistent with reported accounts. 500,000 civilian deaths estimate confirmed.

title: Luwero Triangle Massacres
note: Obote army massacres in Luwero Triangle confirmed; skulls as symbols confirmed; tens of thousands of civilian deaths 1981-1985 documented by human rights organizations.

title: Okello Coup Deposes Obote
note: July 1985 coup by Acholi officers under Tito Okello confirmed; lasted only months before NRA captured Kampala confirmed.

title: Museveni and NRA Capture Kampala
note: NRA captured Kampala January 26, 1986 confirmed; Museveni sworn in January 30, 1986. 'Broad-based administration' framing confirmed.

title: Truth Commission on Human Rights Violations
note: Commission of Inquiry into Violations of Human Rights established by Museveni government confirmed. Few perpetrators faced justice — confirmed pattern.

title: Northern Uganda Insurgency Erupts
note: Post-1986 Acholi insurgency confirmed; UPDA and other groups confirmed. North-south divide rooted in colonial recruitment patterns confirmed.

title: Lord's Resistance Army Founded by Joseph Kony
note: LRA founded 1987-88 confirmed; Alice Lakwena/Holy Spirit Movement connection confirmed; ~66,000 children abducted figure confirmed by HRW and other sources.

title: Economic Liberalization Under IMF Structural Adjustment
note: IMF structural adjustment 1987-88 confirmed; strong growth through 1990s confirmed; Uganda as showcase for market-oriented development confirmed.

title: Uganda Pioneers HIV/AIDS Response
note: Uganda's HIV/AIDS ABC campaign and sustained prevalence decline from ~15% to under 8% widely documented. Global model status confirmed.

title: Traditional Kingdoms Restored
note: 1993 Traditional Institutions Statute confirmed; Kabaka Mutebi II crowned July 1993 confirmed; Buganda, Toro, Bunyoro restored confirmed. Note: Ankole restoration was blocked by Museveni — event omits this nuance.

title: Constituent Assembly Elections
note: March 1994 Constituent Assembly elections confirmed; individual (non-party) candidacy under movement system confirmed.

title: New Constitution Enacted — Movement System Retained
note: October 1995 constitution promulgated confirmed; movement system retention confirmed; described as progressive in structure but not genuine multiparty democracy confirmed.

title: First Presidential Election Under New Constitution
note: May 1996 election confirmed; Museveni ~74% confirmed; Paul Ssemogerere of Democratic Party as challenger confirmed; largely free and fair assessment confirmed.

title: Uganda Intervenes in Congo's Civil War
note: Uganda troops into DRC 1996-97 supporting Kabila confirmed; LRA pursuit and resource extraction confirmed; ICJ ruling on international law violations confirmed.

title: LRA Abduction Campaign Intensifies
note: Mass child abductions and ~1.6-2 million IDP displacement confirmed. Protected camps generating severe humanitarian conditions confirmed.

title: Rwenzori Mountain Massacre by Allied Democratic Forces
note: Year is wrong: the Kichwamba Technical College attack was June 8, 1998, not 1999. Location: Kabarole District (not Kasese); 80 students killed in dormitory fire confirmed; ADF Rwenzori mountains confirmed. The event year should be 1998.

title: Referendum Extends Movement-Only System
note: June 2000 referendum confirmed; ~90% vote for movement system confirmed; opposition boycott confirmed; donor criticism confirmed.

title: Movement for the Restoration of the Ten Commandments Massacre
note: March 17, 2000 confirmed; Kanungu district confirmed. Death toll: 530 in the fire; ~780 total including mass graves. Event states '778 followers' — close to total ~780 but fire alone was 530; conflates fire and mass grave victims.

title: Museveni Re-Elected Amid Opposition Allegations
note: March 2001 election confirmed; Museveni 69% vs Besigye confirmed; Supreme Court found irregularities but declined to annul confirmed.

title: Operation Iron Fist Against LRA
note: Operation Iron Fist March 2002 confirmed; deployment into southern Sudan with Sudanese permission confirmed; failed to eliminate LRA and provoked massive retaliation confirmed.

title: Northern Uganda Humanitarian Crisis Peaks
note: 1.7 million IDP figure confirmed; Jan Egeland 'forgotten humanitarian crisis' statement confirmed; children's nightly commutes ('night commuters') confirmed.

title: Barlonyo Massacre by LRA
note: February 21, 2004 confirmed; Lira district confirmed; death toll 200-300+ confirmed (government said 84, local authorities said ~200, unofficial reports 300-500). Proximity to government forces confirmed.

title: Multiparty System Restored by Referendum
note: July 28, 2005 referendum confirmed; movement system ended confirmed; same amendments removed two-term presidential limit confirmed; Museveni ran for third term in 2006 confirmed.

title: ICC Indicts LRA Leadership
note: Warrants issued July 8, 2005, unsealed October 13, 2005 confirmed; five LRA commanders including Kony confirmed; first ICC arrest warrants ever confirmed. Event says 'four other LRA commanders' — correct (Kony + 4 others = 5 total).

title: Juba Peace Talks with LRA
note: July 2006 start confirmed; South Sudanese (Riek Machar) mediation confirmed; cessation of hostilities August 2006 confirmed; Kony refused to sign April 2008 confirmed; ICC warrants as stated reason confirmed.

title: Museveni Wins Third Term in First Multiparty Election
note: February 2006 election confirmed; Museveni 59% vs Besigye confirmed; Besigye treason/rape charges as politically motivated widely reported; EU mission fell short of standards finding confirmed.

title: Anti-Homosexuality Bill Introduced
note: David Bahati introduced bill October 14, 2009 confirmed; original death penalty provision confirmed; international condemnation confirmed; evangelical influence noted by multiple sources.

title: Kampala Bombings by Al-Shabaab
note: July 11, 2010 confirmed; two venues watching World Cup final confirmed; Al-Shabaab responsibility confirmed; death toll 74-76 (event states 76 — within range); AMISOM as motive confirmed.

title: Walk-to-Work Protests and Crackdown
note: April 2011 protests confirmed; fuel/food price grievances confirmed; Besigye arrested multiple times confirmed; pepper spray incidents confirmed; HRW documented at least 9 killed (event says 'several').

title: Museveni Wins Fourth Presidential Term
note: February 2011 election confirmed; Museveni 68% confirmed; unprecedented campaign spending on state resources confirmed; Commonwealth improvements over 2006 finding confirmed.

title: Invisible Children Kony 2012 Campaign
note: March 5, 2012 release confirmed; 100 million views in 6 days (most viral video at the time) confirmed; debate about advocacy and LRA's diminished size confirmed.

title: Anti-Homosexuality Act Signed into Law
note: Year field is wrong: parliament passed the bill December 20, 2013, but Museveni signed it February 24, 2014 — not 2013. The event description correctly says 'February 2014' but the year field says 2013. Constitutional Court annulled August 1, 2014 on quorum grounds confirmed. Should be year 2014.

title: Constitutional Court Nullifies Anti-Homosexuality Act
note: August 1, 2014 annulment confirmed; procedural quorum grounds confirmed; activists noted temporary relief only confirmed.

title: Museveni Wins Fifth Term Amid Besigye Arrest
note: February 2016 election confirmed; Museveni 60.8% confirmed; Besigye arrested multiple times confirmed; EU/Commonwealth/AU criticism confirmed.

title: Parliament Removes Presidential Age Limit
note: December 20, 2017 vote confirmed; 315 for, 62 against confirmed; soldiers entering chamber and opposition MPs beaten confirmed (MP Betty Nambooze's back broken). Museveni age 73 at time confirmed.

title: EACOP Pipeline Agreement Signed
note: EACOP project involves TotalEnergies and CNOOC confirmed; 1,443 km confirmed; $5+ billion confirmed; displacement concerns confirmed. However, key agreements: InterGovernmental Agreement was May 2017; construction agreements signed April 2021 — no distinct major agreement in 2018. Year 2018 not confirmed as the agreement date.

title: Bobi Wine Emerges as Opposition Leader
note: 2017 by-election victory confirmed; 'People Power' movement confirmed; August 2018 Arua arrest on treason charges confirmed; alleged torture in military detention confirmed. Year 2019 is when he consolidated as leader; events began 2017-2018.

title: COVID-19 Lockdown and Economic Disruption
note: March 2020 lockdown confirmed; Uganda's strict lockdown and school closure confirmed; schools closed nearly two years (one of longest globally) documented by UNICEF and others.

title: Election Campaign Violence — Bobi Wine Crackdown
note: November 2020 protests after Bobi Wine's arrest confirmed; at least 54 killed confirmed by Amnesty (some sources say 37-54 range); thousands arrested confirmed.

title: Museveni Wins Sixth Term — Bobi Wine Claims Fraud
note: January 14, 2021 election confirmed; Museveni 58% confirmed; internet blackout confirmed; observer restrictions confirmed; Wine under house arrest confirmed.

title: Kampala Suicide Bombings
note: Major twin suicide bombings near parliament and police headquarters were November 16, 2021 — not October 23. October 23 was a smaller bar bombing in Komamboga killing one person. Event date is wrong. ADF/Islamic State responsibility confirmed; 4 killed and 33+ wounded (November 16 attack) confirmed.

title: Oil Production Start — Tilenga Project
note: Tilenga project in Albertine Rift confirmed; 6.5 billion barrel reserve estimate confirmed; displacement concerns near Murchison Falls confirmed. However, 'began drilling production wells in 2022' is uncertain — as of 2025 EACOP is ~75-79% complete but first oil has not been achieved. The 2022 drilling start claim lacks clear confirmation.

title: Uganda Hosts One Million South Sudanese Refugees
note: Uganda as Africa's largest refugee host confirmed; 1.5 million+ refugees confirmed; South Sudanese and Congolese as largest groups confirmed; open-door policy with freedom of movement/work rights confirmed.

title: Anti-Homosexuality Act 2023 — Among World's Harshest
note: Signed May 29, 2023 confirmed; death penalty for aggravated homosexuality confirmed; AGOA suspension confirmed; World Bank pause on new public financing confirmed. Among world's harshest characterization confirmed.

title: International Sanctions and Aid Restrictions Over LGBTQ Law
note: US AGOA revocation confirmed; World Bank halt on new direct lending confirmed; EU and bilateral donor reviews confirmed.

title: Ebola Outbreak Sudan Strain Contained
note: Sudan strain outbreak confirmed; 55 deaths / 142 confirmed cases confirmed; onset September 2022, declared over January 11, 2023 confirmed. Note: outbreak began September 2022 not 2023 — event year says 2023 (the containment year) which is acceptable framing.

title: EACOP Construction Advances Amid Protests
note: Construction continuing in 2024 confirmed; European banks/insurers declining confirmed; TotalEnergies proceeding with African/Asian financing confirmed; 75-79% complete as of late 2025 confirmed.

title: Continued Political Repression of Opposition and Media
note: Ongoing arrests of NUP members and opposition confirmed; Freedom House 'Not Free' classification confirmed; systematic harassment documented by multiple human rights organizations.

title: LRA Still Active in Congo Despite Uganda Phase Ending
note: LRA active in CAR and DRC confirmed; greatly reduced from peak confirmed; Kony believed alive in CAR-Sudan border area confirmed; Dominic Ongwen 25-year ICC sentence (2021) confirmed.
